li.label: a tenth of everything
li.description: Every morning a tenth of the silver walks out of the gate. I watched it go, coin by coin.

li.label: tithes
li.description: A tenth of the silver given away each morning. I suppose it's for a good cause.

li.label: giving our tenth
li.description: We give a tenth, the way decent people do. It sits well with me.

li.label: an honest tithe
li.description: We give back from what we've been given. It feels like the colony is right with the world.

li.label: locked in at night
li.description: Barred in my own home at ten like a prisoner. The best hours of the day, gone.

li.label: a curfew
li.description: In by ten, gate barred, lights out. The evenings are very short.

li.label: safe at night
li.description: Everyone in, the gate barred, the watch on the wall. I sleep easier.

li.label: the gate barred
li.description: Nobody out in the dark, nothing coming in. For the first time in weeks I'm not listening for footsteps.

li.label: drilled every evening
li.description: Every evening, spear drill until dark. I came here to get away from this.

li.label: militia drills
li.description: An hour of drill most evenings. I'm sore and I'm not getting any better.

li.label: the evening muster
li.description: An hour on the green with everyone, getting a little better each time.

li.label: a proper militia
li.description: We're starting to look like people who could hold a gate. I'm proud of us.

li.label: food given away
li.description: Our food, handed out at the gate to people who never lifted a finger for it.

li.label: alms at the gate
li.description: Food goes out at the gate every morning. I hope we don't need it ourselves.

li.label: bread at the gate
li.description: Nobody leaves our gate hungry this week. That's a good thing to be able to say.

li.label: feeding the hungry
li.description: A child came back to the gate today just to say thank you. I had to go inside for a while.

li.label: someone else's holy days
li.description: Three days of prayers that aren't mine, and work stopped for every one of them.

li.label: holy days
li.description: Prayers at dawn and dusk, and work set down for them. It's not my way.

li.label: keeping the holy days
li.description: We set down our work for the faith, together. It steadies me.

li.label: the faith kept well
li.description: Three days given to the faith, the whole colony at prayer. I feel closer to what matters than I have in a long time.

li.label: strangers everywhere
li.description: Strangers wandering through the colony, handling everything. I can't wait for them to leave.

li.label: market crowds
li.description: Too many people, too much noise, and somebody always wanting to sell me something.

li.label: market day
li.description: Stalls by the gate, haggling, news from the road. It's good to see new faces.

li.label: a good market
li.description: I got the better of a trader today, and I'm going to be talking about it for a week.

li.label: made to fast
li.description: Two days without a proper meal, by order. I can't think about anything but food.

li.label: fasting
li.description: Water and a little bread at sundown. My stomach has opinions about this.

li.label: a clean fast
li.description: Two days of going without. My head is clear in a way it hasn't been in weeks.

li.label: the fast
li.description: Hungry and light-headed and perfectly calm. I'd forgotten how little I need.

li.label: that song again
li.description: The same four lines from dawn to dusk. I hear them in my sleep.

li.label: singing at work
li.description: Everyone singing while they work. I can't hear myself think.

li.label: a work song
li.description: We sang the whole afternoon through, and the work was done before I noticed.

li.label: singing together
li.description: The whole field singing in time, every hand keeping the beat. I'll remember this.

li.label: kept apart
li.description: Everyone at arm's length, the gate shut, nobody to talk to. It's worse than being ill.

li.label: quarantine
li.description: Keeping our distance, sleeping apart, nobody in or out. It's lonely.

li.label: keeping it out
li.description: The sick apart, the gate shut. Whatever is going round, it isn't getting in here.

li.label: safe behind the gate
li.description: I've seen what a fever does to a town. Here, at least, we're doing it right.

li.label: hungry for strangers
li.description: Half portions for us so strangers can eat. I'm hungry, and I didn't choose this.

li.label: famine bread
li.description: Smaller bowls, and the rest sent down the road to the hungry. I mind it more than I'd like to.

li.label: sharing the lean times
li.description: We eat a little less so others can eat at all. It's the right thing.

li.label: bread for the hungry
li.description: Every sack that goes down the road is someone who lives through the winter. I'd give more.

li.label: the gates left open
li.description: Anyone could walk in. Anyone at all. I keep a knife under my pillow now.

li.label: open gates
li.description: Strangers coming and going all week. I don't like not knowing who's about.

li.label: a welcoming place
li.description: New faces at the gate, news from the road. It feels like we're part of the world again.

li.label: open to the world
li.description: Travellers at supper and stories from far away. This is how a colony should live.
